---
title: "revealjs: absolute positioning"
format: revealjs
# Port of Quarto 1 tests/docs/reveal/mini/absolute.qmd, which had no
# assertions. The position attributes of an `.absolute` Div, Span or Image
# move into its inline style (bare numbers get `px`, units pass through, the
# order is Quarto 1's fixed top/left/bottom/right/width/height) and no
# `data-top`-style attribute is left behind. An author style is kept in front.
_quarto:
  tests:
    revealjs:
      ensureHtmlElements:
        - - 'section img.absolute[style="top: 200px; left: 0px; width: 350px; height: 300px;"]'
          - 'section img.absolute[style="top: 50px; right: 50px; width: 450px; height: 250px;"]'
          - 'section img.absolute[style="bottom: 20px; right: 100px; width: 300px; height: 300px;"]'
          - 'section div.absolute[style="left: 2em; bottom: 10%;"]'
          - 'section span.absolute[style="color: red; top: 0px; right: 0px;"]'
          - 'section p > img.absolute'
        - - '[data-top]'
          - '[data-left]'
          - '[data-bottom]'
          - '[data-right]'
          - 'img.absolute[width]'
          - 'img.absolute[height]'
          - 'img.absolute.r-stretch'
---
